post.author: Shadman Rahman
post.headline: Principal Product Manager, Search, Monetization & Student Experience | 134M users, 60+ markets | Builder PM | MSc HCI
post.text: I had decided my writing here had stopped working.The evidence: three recent posts. 387 impressions, then 356, then 538. A couple of likes each. That felt like a clear downward story and I was ready to act on it. Reshare the old stuff, change the topic, something.Then I exported the actual 365 days instead of reading three data points.Almost everything I believed was wrong.Two posts from one week last August account for 51% of my entire year. Every "normal" I was measuring against was a spike I never repeated.My engagement rate has been steady at 2.0 to 2.3% the whole time. So the writing was not the problem.Reach genuinely has fallen though, about 75% since May, and I would not have believed that from three posts either. I was right that something was broken and wrong about what.The part that stung: my followers are not the people who read me. My follower list skews one way almost entirely. The people the algorithm actually serves my posts to are a different set, in different countries, doing different jobs. I had been writing for the wrong room for months.Three data points gave me a story. The export gave me a different one, and I only have it because checking took twenty minutes instead of a week.What have you concluded lately from three data points?

comments.author: Jahin Showic 1st Snr. Product Manager at Sennder | Driving $1.4Bil+ annual RR in Tech Solutions | Empowering 27+Clients with Strategic Design & Dev Consulting | SaaS | Logistics
comments.text: Shadman Rahman 3 data points are enough to create a narrative, but rarely enough to create confidence.I've seen the same thing happen in product: one bad week becomes "retention is broken," one vocal customer becomes "everyone needs this," & one successful experiment becomes "we found the growth lever."The discipline is knowing when you have a signal vs. when you just have a story.
